message.content:
Now I can see the issue. Looking at the `Merge` function, specifically lines 31-38:

```go
last := &out[len(out)-1]
if next.Start < last.End {
    if next.End > last.End {
        last.End = next.End
    }
    continue
}
out = append(out, next)
```

The condition `if next.Start < last.End` checks if the next interval starts before the current interval ends. This handles overlapping intervals, but for adjacent intervals (where `next.Start == last.End`), this condition is false (`next.Start < last.End` is false when `next.Start == last.End`), so it doesn't merge them.

The test case `{{1, 3}, {3, 5}, {5, 9}}` has intervals that touch end-to-start: 1-3 and 3-5 (where 3 == 3), and 3-5 and 5-9 (where 5 == 5). These should be merged into a single interval 1-9.

The fix is to change the condition from `if next.Start < last.End` to `if next.Start <= last.End` to include adjacent intervals. Let me verify this by looking at the logic more carefully:

Actually, looking at line 32: `if next.Start < last.End` - when `next.Start == last.End`, this is false, so adjacent intervals aren't merged. We need `<=` instead of `<`.

message.content:
Perfect! The tests are now passing. The bug was in the `Merge` function where it only merged overlapping intervals (`next.Start < last.End`) but not adjacent intervals (`next.Start == last.End`). By changing the condition to `next.Start <= last.End`, we now correctly merge both overlapping and adjacent intervals.

The fix is minimal and targeted: just one character change from `<` to `<=` on line 32 of `intervals.go`. All tests pass, including the `TestMergeAdjacent` test that was failing before.
